lastCompletedStory.title: Harden the Loop-header ghost against resize/reflow storms

nextStoryContext: US-002 extracted the resize handler previously inlined in runDashboardInk into an exported factory `makeResizeClearer({ writeFn?, setTimeoutFn?, clearTimeoutFn?, debounceMs? })` (src/commands/dashboard.ts, right before runDashboardInk). It preserves the pre-existing behavior (a single resize still writes an immediate CURSOR.clear before Ink repaints) and additionally arms/re-arms a trailing debounced clear (RESIZE_TRAILING_CLEAR_MS = 100ms) after the last event in a burst, so a rapid reflow storm cannot leave the previous frame's stale line count ghosting the Loop header once the burst settles. `runDashboardInk` now does `const resizeClearer = makeResizeClearer(); process.stdout.on('resize', resizeClearer.onResize);` and calls `resizeClearer.cleanup()` in its cleanup() before removeListener. The timer handle type on ResizeClearerOptions is deliberately `unknown` (never `ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>`): Bun's global `Timer` type and @types/node's ambient `NodeJS.Timeout` are both in scope in this repo (bun-types + @types/node coexist) and produce an overload-resolution conflict ('Timer' vs 'Timeout') if you type the handle concretely; default wiring goes through two tiny single-signature wrapper functions (defaultSetTimeoutFn/defaultClearTimeoutFn) that internally cast just once. Both quality-ratchet files were raised in the same commit with tracker ref #66 (dashboard.ts 893->977, dashboard.test.ts 1467->1582), following the raise-and-retry procedure in patterns.md. Both PRD stories (US-001, US-002) now pass; if this was the last non-operator story, the next actor is the reviewer/orchestrator (this branch's PRD had exactly these two stories, priority 1 and 2, no operator-required entries observed).

officialDocsValidated.summary: Node's tty.WriteStream 'resize' event docs make no debounce/coalescing guarantee (fires whenever columns/rows change, no arguments), confirming that a rapid reflow can legitimately fire multiple 'resize' events in succession and that any debounce/coalescing is the application's responsibility -- which is exactly what makeResizeClearer's trailing-timer hardening implements.
